UX case study

Data insights for a server operating system

Product overview

Open Enterprise Server (OES) is a comprehensive server operating system which securely does storage management, file management, print management and network management. There are multiple services running on OES to enable the above operations. Some of the services are:

  • Novell Storage Services (NSS) - stores, organizes and manages files and directories on a disk
  • Cloud Integrated Storage - migrate/recall hot/cold data based on assigned policies
  • eDirectory - store and manage information about users, devices, and resources on a network
  • File access protocols - NCP, CIFS (client server communication)
  • iPrint - manages the print services in an organization
  • Linux User Management (LUM) - manages the access to LINUX workstations

Problem space

OES is currently managed through multiple interfaces like iManager, iMonitor, Remote manager, NSS management utility, ipcon, PSM status and other command line utilities.

  • Fragmented data on multiple interfaces
  • No estate wide data trend with key filters
  • No hot/cold data trend for top servers/volumes/users
  • Cold data accumulates silently on hot tier
  • Tiering decisions are difficult without proper data insights upfront

Research & Discovery

To build a solution that truly addresses user needs, conducted extensive research with administrators, business analysts and other stakeholders across multiple time zones and industries.

Research methodology

  • 12 in-depth user interviews across 3 time zones
  • Contextual inquiry sessions observing daily workflows
  • Collaborative workshops with product manager and other stakeholders
  • Analysis of existing support tickets and escalation patterns

Participant profiles

Administrators

Manage the infrastructure and trouble shoot the technical issues

Business analysts

Monitor KPIs and generate reports for stakeholders

Pain points

Hot data buried

Active, time-sensitive records were mixed with archival data.

Cold data overwhelm

Historical data had no visual distinction from live data.

No aggregate story

Admins needed a "total health" view but had to mentally sum fragmented widgets.

Persona

Marcus Reid

Senior Server & Storage Administrator & Data Tiering Specialist · Enterprise IT · 11 years experience

Storage Management OES data tiering Access pattern analysis Storage cost optimisation NSS volume analytics
"Every byte on my fastest SAN costs 12× what it costs on nearline. I need to see exactly which data is hot, which is cold, and why - so I can move the right data to the right tier before it costs us."

Hot tier - SSD

Actively accessed data; high IOPS demand. Finance, HR active files, database volumes.

~18%of total · highest cost/GB

Cold tier - Nearline

Rarely accessed; compliance & audit data, yearly backups, legacy project files.

~40%of total · lowest cost/GB

Goals

  • ✓
    Identify which volumes & files are hot vs coldPer-volume access frequency heatmap across all 24 servers
  • ✓
    Automate cold data migration to less expensive storagePolicy-driven tiering: if not accessed in 90 days → move
  • ✓
    Reduce hot-tier costs by 30% this fiscal yearMove misclassified cold data off expensive SSD pools
  • ✓
    Justify tiering decisions to leadershipCost-savings reports linking access data to storage spend

Pain points

  • !
    OES has no native access-frequency trackingNo built-in last-access timestamp analytics per volume or file
  • !
    Manual tiering decisions are guessworkWithout access data, moves are based on file age alone - unreliable
  • !
    No cross-server tier utilization viewCan't see hot/cold breakdown across top servers at once
  • !

Empathy map

Sees

  • iManager showing volume sizes - but no access frequency or temperature data
  • OES Health Monitor with point-in-time snapshots, no historical trend for data access
  • Growing SSD pool utilisation month-on-month with no easy way to identify culprits
  • Industry peers using modern object storage platforms with built-in tiering intelligence
  • Management dashboards that show storage cost - but not why costs are rising

Pains

  • No native last-access analytics in OES - must build from raw filesystem timestamps manually
  • Tiering decisions made on file age alone - risky when periodic-access files appear "cold"
  • No cross-server hot/cold heatmap - can't see the full picture without stitching data manually
  • Cost justification reports are built entirely in Excel - time-consuming and error-prone
  • Risk of migrating data that looks cold but has periodic spikes (quarter-end, year-end access)

Gains

  • Native access-frequency heatmap - see hot vs cold at a glance across all 24 servers
  • Tiering policy simulator - preview migration impact and cost savings before executing
  • Periodic access detection - flag volumes with infrequent but recurring access spikes
  • Auto-generated cost-per-tier report - linked to real access data, exportable to PDF/CSV
  • Credibility with leadership - data-backed proof that his tiering work saves measurable cost

Thinks & feels

  • "Cold data sitting on hot-tier SSD is money burning every single day."
  • Anxious that tiering decisions based on file age alone may be wrong - age ≠ temperature
  • Frustrated that he can't prove ROI on tiering to leadership without manual Excel reports
  • Proud when a tiering policy reduces SSD footprint noticeably - feels like real engineering
  • Worried about unintentionally migrating data that looks cold but gets accessed at quarter-end

Hears

  • Finance: "Our storage costs went up 18% - what are you doing about it?"
  • IT Director: "Can you show me a report on where our storage money is going?"
  • Users: "Why is my file access slow?" (hot-tier pool is saturated)
  • Peers: "We moved to object storage for cold data - are you considering that?"
  • Compliance: "Year-end audit files must be retained on accessible storage for 7 years"

Says & does

  • Runs custom `find` scripts every Monday to pull last-access timestamps across volumes
  • Maintains a personal Excel tracker mapping volumes to tiers and last-migration dates
  • Says: "I know the data, I just can't visualise it fast enough to act on it"
  • Manually builds cost-savings slides for monthly IT leadership meetings
  • Advocates internally for a native tiering analytics feature in OES tooling

Solution

A proactive dashboard that clearly gives all the necessary information in a structured way to the user.

✓

An estate wide data on the number of servers, files, volumes, space and migrated data.

✓

Trend of estate wide hot/cold data with key filters.

✓

Trend of top data transactions based on volumes, servers, owners and file types.

Information architecture

Design process

Conducted weekly design reviews with product managers, engineering leads and other key stakeholders. Incorporated feedback rapidly to ensure alignment with both user needs and technical feasibility.

Sketches

I began with quick sketches, translating raw thoughts into simple visuals. These rough outlines captured the essence of the concept and allowed me to explore multiple directions without constraints. They were the playground where creativity flowed freely.

Low-fidelity designs

From sketches, I moved into low-fidelity wireframes. Here, the focus shifted to layout, hierarchy, and user flow. Stripped of colors and polish, these designs emphasized usability and helped me validate the core interactions before investing in detail.

High-fidelity designs

Finally, I refined the concept into high-fidelity prototypes. With typography, color palettes, imagery, and micro-interactions in place, these designs closely resembled the final product. They showcased not just functionality, but the emotional tone and brand personality of the experience.

Cross functional collaboration

Close collaboration with the engineering team was essential to ensure design feasibility while pushing the boundaries of what was technically possible. Established a continuous feedback loop that influenced both design and implementation decisions.

Feasibility alignment

Regular design-engineering sync sessions to validate technical feasibility before committing to the design directions.

  • Weekly technical feasibility reviews
  • API capability assessments
  • Performance constraint planning

User testing & feedback

Conducted multiple rounds of usability testing with real users to validate our design decisions, uncover issues and gather insights for refinement before final development.

Testing methodology

Participants

  • 7 server administrators from 4 companies
  • Mix of novice and expert users
  • Various industries: Universities, Broadcasting, Healthcare

Testing format

  • Moderated remote usability tests
  • Task-based scenarios with think-aloud protocol
  • Post task surveys
